channel.title: The Dayly Guide
channel.description: Practical, evidence-aware writing on family organisation, responsibility and children's independence.

item.title: How to reduce the mental load
item.description: Mental load is not the number of tasks you do. It is how much of family life you are continually keeping track of — and that is what has to change.

item.title: How to help children build good study habits
item.description: The techniques with the best evidence, the ones students actually use, and how to close the gap between them.

item.title: The best chore apps for families
item.description: What to look for in a chore app, why most stop being used by week six, and the design choices that decide whether one lasts.

item.title: The best family organisation apps
item.description: An honest comparison of the main categories of family organisation app, what each is genuinely good at, and where Dayly fits.

item.title: Organising sports and after-school clubs
item.description: Kit, fees, fixtures, lifts and the bag that never gets emptied. A system for the busiest part of family logistics.

item.title: School bag organisation
item.description: A bag that can be packed in two minutes: fixed places for fixed things, a short list, and an unpack habit at the door.

item.title: How to raise considerate children
item.description: Consideration is noticing other people. It is taught by being needed, by seeing it modelled, and by having the effects of your actions pointed out.

item.title: How to remember school deadlines
item.description: Forms, money, trips, projects and dress-up days: why they get missed and the capture habit that fixes almost all of it.

item.title: What children should be responsible for on holiday
item.description: A holiday is a week of practice at running your own life, in a place where the stakes are low. What to hand over, by age.

item.title: School morning routines that actually work
item.description: Work backwards from the leave time, move everything possible to the night before, and give each child a list they can follow without you.

item.title: Back-to-school organisation: a four-week plan
item.description: What to do four weeks, two weeks, one week and one day before term starts — and what to hand over to the children.

item.title: The teen independence checklist
item.description: Practical, financial, domestic and social competences to build between 13 and 18 — and roughly when to start each.

item.title: Family travel documents checklist
item.description: Everything to check before a family trip, when to check it, and the passport rules that catch people out.

item.title: How to teach children manners
item.description: Manners are learned by modelling, practice and age-appropriate expectation — not by correction in public.

item.title: Beach holiday packing list for families
item.description: What to pack for a family beach holiday, what to buy when you arrive, and the beach bag that gets packed once and stays packed.

item.title: How to teach children to keep track of their belongings
item.description: Lost jumpers, water bottles and coats are a systems problem. What actually reduces losses, and what to do when something goes for good.

item.title: Ski holiday packing list for families
item.description: A complete ski packing list by category, what to hire rather than buy for growing children, and what children can pack themselves.

item.title: Laundry: what children can do, and when
item.description: From basket to wardrobe, the stages of handing over washing — and the two rules that stop it becoming a permanent floor problem.

item.title: The best language learning apps for children
item.description: What language apps do well, what they cannot do, and how to use one so a child actually ends up able to speak.

item.title: Homework and teenagers: what changes
item.description: The work matters more, your leverage is lower, and sleep becomes a variable. What to change between 13 and 18.

item.title: How to teach children to break big tasks into steps
item.description: "Clean your room" is not one job. Why children stall on tasks they can do, and how to help them find a first step small enough to start.

item.title: The best maths apps for children
item.description: What to look for in a maths app, which types work for which children, and the questions to ask before subscribing to anything.

item.title: Packing lists by age
item.description: What each age can pack, what they should carry, and what stays on the adult list.

item.title: Holiday and weekend routines
item.description: Keep three anchors, drop everything else, and avoid the Sunday-night cliff back into term time.

item.title: How to motivate children without bribing them
item.description: The difference between a bribe, a reward and a consequence — and six alternatives that work better than all three.

item.title: How to get children to pack their own bags
item.description: A four-stage handover, an age-appropriate list, and the rule that makes it stick: whatever is not packed does not come.

item.title: How to make chores less of a battle
item.description: Seven changes that reduce conflict about household jobs, and the one conversation worth having when the argument is not really about the job.

item.title: How to help children plan long-term school projects
item.description: Projects fail on the day they are set, not the night before. A five-step method for turning a deadline into a sequence.

item.title: What actually motivates children?
item.description: Three conditions with a solid research base — autonomy, competence and relatedness — and what each looks like at a kitchen table.

item.title: Bedtime routines that hold, from toddler to teen
item.description: What changes at each age, why the last twenty minutes should be boring, and how to handle the teenage phone question.

item.title: How to help a messy child become more organised
item.description: Mess is usually a storage problem, not a character problem. Fix where things live before you try to change the child.

item.title: Family travel organisation: how to make the holiday belong to everyone
item.description: A timeline from eight weeks out to the morning of departure, a packing system per person, and the parts children should be doing themselves.

item.title: How to raise responsible children
item.description: Responsibility is built from ownership, visibility, consequence and time. The four conditions, what undermines each, and what to expect at every stage.

item.title: How to stop homework becoming a nightly battle
item.description: When homework is damaging your evenings and your relationship, the answer is usually to make it smaller, not to push harder.

item.title: Teaching children to clean their own rooms
item.description: An agreed standard, a short list and a daily reset beat a weekly battle. What to insist on and what to let go.

item.title: How to teach children about consequences
item.description: Natural consequences teach quickly and cost you nothing. Added punishments teach a child about you. Here is how to tell them apart and use the first.

item.title: How to give children more independence without losing control
item.description: Widening a child’s world in deliberate, practised steps — and the difference between a risk and a discomfort.

item.title: The mental load checklist
item.description: A printable list of the invisible work of running a family, by area. Go through it separately, compare, and find out what only one of you was tracking.

item.title: The Sunday reset
item.description: Thirty minutes that stops a week compounding: look ahead, sort the kit, plan the food, and let everyone see what is coming.

item.title: How to teach children to think ahead
item.description: Most morning problems began the evening before. How to move the noticing from the parent to the child, one step at a time.

item.title: How to create a homework routine that holds
item.description: Same time, same place, food first, and a defined end. The five components of a routine that survives a term, and how to hand it over.

item.title: How to stop doing everything for your child
item.description: You are faster, and that is exactly the problem. A staged method for withdrawing help without a standoff.

item.title: Family chore systems that survive a busy term
item.description: Four common systems compared — rotas, ownership, area-based and points — with the failure mode of each and how to combine them.

item.title: Should children be paid for chores?
item.description: Paying for household jobs changes what they mean. Here is what the research on rewards and motivation actually shows, and a split that works in practice.

item.title: Do reward charts work?
item.description: Sticker charts work briefly and then stop. Here is why, what the research on rewards actually shows, and what to use instead.

item.title: Retrieval practice, explained for parents
item.description: One of the best-supported findings in learning science, in a form you can use at a kitchen table in ten minutes.

item.title: Family evening routines
item.description: The evening is where tomorrow gets decided. A short sequence that removes most morning problems and hands the preparation to the children.

item.title: Why children forget everything
item.description: It is rarely carelessness. Four mechanisms explain most childhood forgetting — and each one points at a different fix.

item.title: How to stop reminding your child about everything
item.description: Reminders feel like help and function like a subscription. A staged plan for replacing your voice with something a child can check themselves.

item.title: What is the mental load?
item.description: The invisible work of noticing, remembering and deciding for a household — what it is, why it lands on one person, and what actually shifts it.
